blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Undoing Differentiation
blocks.content: If differentiation finds the gradient (slope) of a curve, **Integration** does the exact opposite: it takes the gradient formula and works backwards to find the original curve. It's also the tool for finding the area under a curve. Think of differentiation as taking a photo apart pixel by pixel; integration is putting those pixels back together to rebuild the picture.

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: The Power Rule (Reversed)
blocks.content:
The reverse of the differentiation power rule:

• If dy/dx = x^n, then y = x^(n+1) / (n+1) + C.
• **Raise the power by 1**, then **divide by the new power**.
• ALWAYS add the constant of integration **+ C** at the end!
• The integral of a constant k is kx + C.

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: Integrating a Polynomial
blocks.content:
To integrate f(x) = 6x^2 + 4x - 3:

1. Take each term separately.
2. For 6x^2: raise power (2+1=3), divide by new power: 6x^3/3 = 2x^3.
3. For 4x: raise power (1+1=2), divide: 4x^2/2 = 2x^2.
4. For -3: integrate as -3x.
5. Combine and add C: **2x^3 + 2x^2 - 3x + C**.

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Definite Integration
blocks.content:
Find the area under y = x^2 from x = 1 to x = 3.

**Step 1:** Integrate: x^3/3.
**Step 2:** Evaluate at limits: [3^3/3] - [1^3/3] = 27/3 - 1/3 = 9 - 1/3 = 26/3.

**Final Answer: Area = 26/3 = 8.67 square units (2 d.p.).**
(Note: No + C needed for definite integrals!)

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: Two massive traps: (1) Forgetting the + C in indefinite integrals. This is worth a mark in every exam and students throw it away constantly. (2) Getting the power rule backwards. In integration, you ADD 1 to the power and DIVIDE. In differentiation, you SUBTRACT 1 and MULTIPLY. Mixing them up gives you the derivative, not the integral!
